observations.statement: The shortcut runtime is specified as one override-precedence KeyMap used by all key events, with the Shortcuts GUI updating configuration and rebuilding the map immediately; rebuild points include startup, edit/reset, and successful import.
Missing or invalid shortcut configuration falls back to empty overrides, and duplicate bindings are stated as rejected during edit and import validation.

The PM-native skill lifecycle includes discovery, tool-reference-aware validation, pre-launch readiness, compiled-context bundling, on-demand retrieval through the PM skill tool, and optional provider-native interoperability layers.

Projection and drift state are per target; direct editing changes only the selected target to Manual Override, sibling targets are insulated from repair, and projection failure is distinct from PM-native runtime-delivery failure.
The required user-facing capability set includes shortcut filtering, skill bulk permissions, skill sorting/filtering, load-on-demand preview, modified-time display, and validate-all results.

The cleanup checklist defines separate pre-execution and post-execution responsibilities, wraps the platform loop, forbids git-clean during post-execution cleanup, limits agent-output clearing to directory contents, and excludes evidence pruning from post-execution cleanup.

The stated readiness is readiness to produce a detailed implementation plan, while platform-specific skill delivery remains dependent on platform_specs and may be stubbed until that dependency is defined.

candidate_findings.title: Platform modifier normalization lacks a canonical storage boundary
candidate_findings.problem: The macOS rule allows modifier mapping while reading configuration, writing configuration, or displaying the GUI, without selecting which boundary owns the conversion.
candidate_findings.consequence: Equivalent bindings can serialize, display, and compare differently across platforms, affecting portability and conflict detection.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The canonical stored modifier vocabulary, conversion direction, conversion stage, and round-trip behavior are not fixed.

candidate_findings.title: Modifier-free shortcut capture remains behaviorally open
candidate_findings.problem: The recording flow permits either rejecting an unmodified key or allowing it, including possible F-key handling.
candidate_findings.consequence: The same recorded input can be accepted or rejected by different implementations.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The accepted modifier-free key classes and their validation behavior are not selected.

candidate_findings.title: Duplicate-binding resolution has two incompatible outcomes
candidate_findings.problem: Duplicate bindings are required to be prevented, but the specified recording and import paths still allow either rejection or stealing the binding from another action.
candidate_findings.consequence: A conflicting edit or import can either leave existing assignments intact or silently remove one, producing materially different state transitions.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The authoritative duplicate-resolution operation and its state mutation semantics are not fixed.

candidate_findings.title: Shortcut export payload is not fixed
candidate_findings.problem: Export may serialize current overrides only or the full resolved key map.
candidate_findings.consequence: Replace imports can either preserve destination defaults or freeze source-machine defaults into imported data.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The required export payload and the interpretation of default-derived bindings are not selected.

candidate_findings.title: Shortcut version compatibility policy contains competing branches
candidate_findings.problem: The versioning decision says missing or newer versions are rejected, while the same text also permits an implementation-selected best-effort parse for an unknown version.
candidate_findings.consequence: The same file can be rejected by one implementation and partially accepted by another.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The handling of a missing version and every unsupported version is not singularly defined.

candidate_findings.title: Unknown shortcut action IDs lack one import outcome
candidate_findings.problem: An unknown action may be skipped while known actions are imported, or may reject the entire import.
candidate_findings.consequence: Imported state and user-visible success differ for the same input file.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Unknown-action handling, partial-import status, and reported imported count are not fixed.

candidate_findings.title: First-wins skill discovery lacks an exact ordered root list
candidate_findings.problem: First-wins behavior is declared, but project/global and provider-root ordering is given only through examples.
candidate_findings.consequence: Duplicate skill names can resolve to different files depending on builder-selected search order.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The complete ordered DRY:DATA:skill_search_paths value is not present in the capsule.

candidate_findings.title: Partial skill-directory collision behavior remains undecided
candidate_findings.problem: Creation is blocked when an existing directory contains SKILL.md, but an existing directory without SKILL.md may be treated as an error or partial state.
candidate_findings.consequence: Identical filesystem state can either block creation or be modified by creation.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The exact behavior for an existing target directory without SKILL.md is not selected.

candidate_findings.title: Concurrent skill-edit conflict behavior remains undecided
candidate_findings.problem: Saving after an external file change may overwrite with a warning, prompt among reload/overwrite/cancel, or use locking.
candidate_findings.consequence: External edits can be lost, preserved, or block the save depending on implementation.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Change detection, conflict presentation, and permitted save transitions are not fixed.

candidate_findings.title: Ask permission is first-class but its runtime transition is deferred
candidate_findings.problem: Runtime readiness depends on permission state and the bulk UI can assign Ask, while Ask prompting is deferred and its exact UI location is left open.
candidate_findings.consequence: A skill in Ask state has no singular current behavior when a runner is about to load it.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The present-phase readiness result, launch blocking behavior, prompt timing, and persistence effect for Ask are not defined.

candidate_findings.title: Precedence among multiple matching permission patterns is absent
candidate_findings.problem: The only declared precedence is explicit per-skill entry over pattern; no rule orders two or more matching patterns.
candidate_findings.consequence: A skill matched by conflicting patterns can resolve to different permissions.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Pattern-versus-pattern ordering, specificity, and tie behavior are not defined.

candidate_findings.title: Validate-all coverage is unclear for required and optional tool references
candidate_findings.problem: Backend validation must distinguish required_tool_refs from optional_tool_refs and surface exact failures, but validate-all enumerates only frontmatter, name, directory-name match, and description checks.
candidate_findings.consequence: A skill with a blocking required-tool reference problem may appear OK in validate-all while being non-runnable in readiness.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Validate-all inclusion and status rendering for required_tool_refs and optional_tool_refs are not stated.

candidate_findings.title: Validate-all presentation has conflicting acceptance scope
candidate_findings.problem: The text declares a full table as the decision and later acceptance, but also permits an errors-only modal for v1.
candidate_findings.consequence: An implementation may omit successful skills despite the stated full-table acceptance behavior.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Whether the full table is mandatory in v1 or deferrable is not singularly stated.

candidate_findings.title: Skill import does not define post-copy validation failure state
candidate_findings.problem: Import copies a folder into a discovery base and validates name and frontmatter after the copy, but no resulting filesystem state is specified when validation fails.
candidate_findings.consequence: A failed import can leave a partial or invalid skill in a discovery path, or can be rolled back, depending on implementation.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Atomicity, cleanup, discoverability, and user-visible status after post-copy validation failure are not defined.

candidate_findings.title: Frontmatter name mismatch still has two save behaviors
candidate_findings.problem: The name must match the directory, but save may either reject the change or offer to rename the folder.
candidate_findings.consequence: The same edit can fail without mutation or rename the skill's filesystem identity.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The v1 save transition for a changed frontmatter name is not fixed.

candidate_findings.title: Skill sort persistence scope is ambiguous
candidate_findings.problem: The last-chosen sort may be stored only for the session or in GuiConfig.
candidate_findings.consequence: Sort selection may reset after restart or persist across opens.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The persistence lifetime and authoritative storage location for the sort preference are not selected.

candidate_findings.title: Skill preview representation is not singular
candidate_findings.problem: The preview may show the markdown body only or the full file with collapsed frontmatter.
candidate_findings.consequence: Frontmatter visibility and copyable content differ between conforming implementations.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The exact preview content model and frontmatter visibility are not fixed.

candidate_findings.title: Projection state storage lacks an exact state model
candidate_findings.problem: Projection and drift state must be stored per target, and Manual Override is named, but target identity, allowed state values, drift values, and transition triggers are not enumerated in the capsule.
candidate_findings.consequence: Projection status, drift detection, and selected-target repair can be represented and transitioned incompatibly.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The projection_targets schema and complete per-target state machine are not defined here.

candidate_findings.title: Shortcut import persistence failure is not state-defined
candidate_findings.problem: Successful import rebuilds the key map and persists configuration, but the operation order and failure state are not stated when persistence fails.
candidate_findings.consequence: An unsaved imported binding set may remain active in memory or may be rolled back, yielding different visible and restart behavior.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The transaction boundary, rollback behavior, and error-visible state for import persistence failure are not defined.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Corrupt or structurally invalid shortcut configuration has an explicit non-crashing fallback to empty overrides, warning logging, a named toast, and a default-derived key map.
Shortcut filtering explicitly distinguishes an empty query from a non-empty query with no matches.
Explicit per-skill permission entries explicitly override pattern entries.
Import from path explicitly copies into a discovery base and does not persist arbitrary external paths.
Creating a skill with no open project explicitly offers only a global target and removes the project option.
MVP runtime delivery explicitly uses the canonical registry, permission filtering, context bundling, and the skill tool rather than requiring a provider-native delivery matrix.
Validate-all explicitly continues after an unreadable skill and reports that skill as an error rather than aborting the run.
Direct edits and repair are explicitly isolated to the selected projection target, and projection failure is explicitly distinct from PM-native runtime-delivery failure.
Post-execution cleanup explicitly excludes git-clean, clearing agent output preserves the directory itself, and evidence pruning is excluded from cleanup_after_execution.
The readiness claim is explicitly limited to producing a detailed implementation plan, and the unresolved platform-specific skill-delivery dependency is explicitly identified.

unknowns.why_unresolved_within_capsule: The capsule names the external canonical skill system but does not include that contract's contents.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote: Merge defaults with overrides (overrides take precedence).
If supporting macOS, map Ctrl -> Cmd and Alt -> Option when reading/writing config or displaying in GUI; do this in one place (same DRY data or a small platform module).
All key events (e.g. in composer, prompt fields) go through this map to resolve to `ShortcutAction` then execute the corresponding behavior.

On "Change", record new key combo, validate (no duplicate action binding; optional conflict check), update GuiConfig.shortcuts and persist; then rebuild key map so the new binding is active immediately.
**Key map rebuild:** (1) On app startup after loading GuiConfig; (2) After user saves a change on the Shortcuts screen (edit or reset); (3) After successful import (Replace or Merge).

If shortcuts section is missing, use empty overrides. If it fails to parse or is invalid, fall back to empty overrides, log warning, show toast "Shortcuts reset to defaults due to config error" (§7.11).
discover skills from PM roots plus compatible import roots defined by the canonical skill system.

validate `SKILL.md` frontmatter, including `required_tool_refs` and `optional_tool_refs`; `required_tool_refs` problems block runnable `/readiness`, `optional_tool_refs` problems warn, and the Skills `GUI` surfaces the exact failing refs instead of flattening them into one generic error.
compute runtime readiness before launch from validation state, permission state, and tool availability.
bundle PM-selected skill content into the compiled context.
expose the PM `skill` tool for on-demand skill retrieval during the run.
treat provider-native skill directories and file formats as optional import/export/projection layers only.

projection state and drift state must be tracked per target through `projection_targets` / `projection_targets[]`; target families may include workspace `AGENTS.md`, workspace `CLAUDE.md`, workspace `GEMINI.md`, workspace `.cursor/rules/pm-generated.mdc`, workspace `cursor/rules/pm-generated.mdc`, and provider/account-local `/account-local` config references where needed.
editing a provider-native projection target directly requires switching only that target to `Manual Override`; repair acts on the chosen target and must not silently revert sibling targets.
a projection failure does not mean PM-native skill runtime delivery failed.
if user presses a key with no modifier, either reject with tooltip "Use a modifier (Ctrl/Alt/Cmd)" or allow (e.g. F-keys).
"No duplicate action binding" is required.

if the key combo is already bound to a *different* action, either (a) **reject** with tooltip "Already used by <ActionName>" and do not save, or (b) **steal** (assign to new action and remove from old); implementation must decide.

**fall back to defaults** (empty overrides), log a warning, and **show a toast** ("Shortcuts reset to defaults due to config error"). Do not crash; key map = `build_key_map(default_shortcuts(), empty_overrides)`.

On import, if `version` is missing or greater than the highest supported version, **reject** with message "Unsupported shortcut file version" (or "implementation must decide": skip unknown version and attempt to parse known fields for best-effort import).

**Empty filter** = show all shortcut rows. **Non-empty filter with no matches** = show empty list and a single inline message (e.g. "No shortcuts match 'xyz'") so the user can tell "no match" from "no data."
Discovery walks paths in a defined order (e.g. project paths first, then global; within each, e.g. `.puppet-master/skills` then `.claude/skills` then `.agents/skills`).
Implementation must decide whether to treat "dir exists but no SKILL.md" as error or as partial state (e.g. offer to create SKILL.md only).

on save: (1) overwrite and warn "File was modified on disk; your version was saved", or (2) detect mtime/content change and prompt "File changed on disk. Reload / Overwrite / Cancel", or (3) lock file for v1 (complex).

**Decision:** Show a **full table** (all discovered skills) with a status column: OK or Error + message. This allows users to see which skills passed and which failed in one view. Summary line: "N OK, M errors." Optional: filter toggle "Show only errors" to collapse to errors-only. Implementation plan may choose errors-only modal for v1 if full table is deferred.
**Defer to later:** "Ask" means prompt user before an agent loads the skill.
When resolving permission for a skill name, check explicit entries in `skill_permissions` first; if none match, then apply pattern rules (e.g. `doc-*: allow`).

"Import" means: user picks an existing folder containing `SKILL.md`; we copy that folder into a chosen discovery base (e.g. `.puppet-master/skills/<name>` or `~/.config/puppet-master/skills/<name>`). We do not persist arbitrary external paths (keeps discovery simple and portable). Validate name and frontmatter after copy.
When no project is open (no project root), "Create new" skill: offer **global only** (e.g. `~/.config/puppet-master/skills/<name>`). Disable or hide "project" option when `project_root` is None.

On save, if user changes `name` in frontmatter so it no longer matches the dir name: (1) reject with validation error "Name must match folder name", or (2) offer "Rename folder" to rename dir to match (then save).

MVP runtime delivery uses the canonical registry + permission filter + context bundling + `skill` tool path. Provider-native formats may be documented as interoperability inputs, but implementation does not require a separate per-provider native runtime delivery matrix.
Serialize current overrides only (or full key map) to JSON.
On success, rebuild key map and persist; toast "Imported N shortcuts."
Unknown action id in file → skip or reject entire import; document to skip unknown and import known only, or reject with "Unknown action: X".
if invalid, reject with "Conflict: key already used by <Action>" or apply and steal; implementation must decide
on import, if version > supported, reject with "Unsupported shortcut file version."

User enters pattern (e.g. `doc-*`) and selects Allow/Deny/Ask; Apply shows confirmation with count; on confirm, config is updated and persisted; list reflects new permissions; explicit per-skill overrides pattern (see precedence below).
**Explicit per-skill wins over pattern** (so "doc-release" with explicit "deny" is still denied when pattern "doc-*" is allow).

User can sort by Name, Source, or Permission; filter by text (name/description), source (All / Project / Global), and permission (All / Allow / Deny / Ask); combined filters apply; sort preference persists (session or GuiConfig).
Store last-chosen sort in session or in GuiConfig (e.g. `skills_list_sort: "name" | "source" | "permission"`) so it persists across opens.

Selecting a skill in the list shows its body in a read-only pane (Skills tab); content is load-on-demand; user can copy text; "Edit" opens full editor. If load fails (missing file, invalid frontmatter), show error in pane instead of body.
Content = markdown body only (no frontmatter), or full file with frontmatter collapsed.
List shows last modified (date or relative) per skill; preview pane can show same; optional version from frontmatter if we extend it.

User clicks "Validate all" on Skills tab; all discovered skills are validated; results show in a full table (all skills) with status OK or Error + message; summary "N OK, M errors"; errors are copy-pasteable (selectable labels).
On click, run validation for every discovered skill (same rules as load_skill: frontmatter, name 1-64 chars and regex, name matches dir, description 1-1024 chars).
`validate_skill(path: &Path) -> Result<(), ValidationError>` (DRY:FN) that reads SKILL.md, parses frontmatter, checks name and description and dir-name match; returns Ok(()) or Err with message.
If a skill path becomes unreadable during validate-all, show Error with message (e.g. "Could not read file"); do not abort entire run -- continue and report per-skill.
The spec (§7.7-§7.10) plus this subsection (§7.11) and checklists (§8.8, §8.9) are **sufficient for an implementer to produce a detailed implementation plan** for Puppet Master.

Define Slint key-event integration point: where key events are captured (window vs focused widget, via `FocusScope` or window-level handler) and how KeyMap is applied; document in implementation plan (per §7.11 "Slint key event wiring").
Confirm platform_specs (or orchestrator plan) documents how each platform receives skill list (paths vs content; CLI env vs prompt injection); implementation plan references this per platform.
platform_specs (or equivalent) for skill injection per platform when integrating Skills with runners.
Skills backend can stub `list_skills_for_agent` until orchestrator and platform_specs define how runners receive the skill list.
Implement `cleanup_exclude_patterns()` (or `CLEANUP_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS`) with exact list from §4.8; tag DRY:DATA.

implement `prepare_working_directory(work_dir, config)` per §4.8 step-by-step (git check → skip if not repo; optional reset omitted; call run_git_clean_with_excludes if config.untracked; optional agent-output clear)
implement `cleanup_after_execution(pid, work_dir, config)` per §4.8 (terminate process; runner temp only; optional build-artifact dirs); tag DRY:FN. Do **not** call run_git_clean_with_excludes here.

call `prepare_working_directory(&context.working_directory, &cleanup_config)` before the platform loop; then call `runner.execute(request)` directly (CLI-only — `execute_with_sdk_fallback` has been removed); then call `cleanup_after_execution(0, &context.working_directory, &cleanup_config)` after it returns.
Confirm cleanup_after_execution never calls run_git_clean_with_excludes; only prepare_working_directory and manual "Clean workspace" do.
if config.clear_agent_output, clear contents of agent_output_dir(work_dir) only; do not remove the dir.
call from manual action or background, not from cleanup_after_execution.
One variant per row in the default table in §7.7.
`default_shortcuts() -> Vec<(ShortcutAction, KeyBinding)>` (or `HashMap<ShortcutAction, KeyBinding>`) as the single source of truth.
